newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak steel company VSZ pushes SAX index higher.
newsitem.headline: Slovak steel company VSZ pushes SAX index higher.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed in quiet trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with brokers saying the market was rising on the perception that Slovak shares are seriously undervalued.
The SAX index firmed 1.75 points to a year high of 207.75 points.
"The Slovak market is incredibly cheap at the moment, compared with those in neighbouring countries," Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt said.
Krutil said VSZ, currently the most liquid listed share on BSE, along with Slovnaft and Slovakofarma were the three major issues supporting the market, while other issues were being largely ignored.
VSZ closed down eight crowns at 720, but its average price traded 1.2 percent higher, on volume of 9,845 shares.

"The price of VSZ has been supported by large blocks and there are also big packages of the issue offered on the O-T-C (over the counter) market," Krutil said. "It seems that both the holders and buyers in VSZ have been satisfied by the same price level."
Overall, volume increased to 395,704 shares, from 364,041 shares traded on Monday, while turnover eased to 290.41 million crowns, from 338.9 million.
